Scoring: Dukes 2 touchdowns and 1 field goal; Huskies 5 touchdowns and 2 field goals. The last score: C. Bowers run for 17 yds, for a TD (M. Baker KICK) (4th quarter, 2:39).

Leading the way — Dukes: JC Evans 27/42, 236 yds, 1 TD, 1 INT, 17 car, 49 yds, 2 TD; Braeden Wisloski 7 rec, 75 yds, 1 TD. Huskies: Kalieb Osborne 16/20, 274 yds, 3 TD; Cyncir Bowers 25 car, 123 yds, 2 TD; Shamar Porter 4 rec, 135 yds, 1 TD.
Where Huskies won it: they outgained them 504 yards to 331, won the turnover battle (0 to 1) and held the ball 31:53 to 28:07.

Against the closing line (Draft Kings): Dukes closed as 4.5-point favorites and lost outright to Huskies; Huskies won as the underdog at +164; the total closed at 56.5 and they combined for 68, over by 11.5.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 14, 11:57 AM ET. It had Dukes 75% and Huskies 25%, projecting Dukes 33.3 – Huskies 23 (56.3 total, Dukes by 10.3).

Final: Dukes 22 – Huskies 46. Wrong winner: it had Dukes at 75%, and Huskies (25%) won.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Dukes came in with a 10% above average attack and a 9% stingier than average defense (8-2, 40.6 scored and 19.3 allowed a game over 10 games), worth about 176 and 173 games of evidence. Projected to score 33.3, they scored 22 (−11.3 points, 34% under); projected to allow 23, they allowed 46 (+23 points, 100% over).

Huskies came in with a 9% below average attack and a 11% leakier than average defense (4-5, 32.9 scored and 26.7 allowed a game over 9 games), worth about 173 and 173 games of evidence. Projected to score 23, they scored 46 (+23 points, 100% over); projected to allow 33.3, they allowed 22 (−11.3 points, 34% under).

The bigger miss was Huskies' scoring (+23 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 68 against 56.3 projected (+11.7), about the 77th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±15.5).

Margin: Huskies by 24 against Dukes by 10.3 projected, about the 99th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±15.3).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Market (Line movement signal): Huskies ×1.00, Dukes ×1.02. It favored Dukes, who did not beat their projection by more than the other side did.

review.title: Where the public and the money were
review.body:
Splits (Action Network): spread: 77% of bets on Dukes, 69% of the money — Huskies covered; total: 53% of bets on the over, 68% of the money — it went over; moneyline: 93% of bets on Dukes, 94% of the money.

The sharp side by the algo's read was Dukes, who lost and didn't cover.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×1.161 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +32.8 points. It counts toward CFB scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 78 graded CFB games the algo now scales scoring ×0.962 and gives home teams -1.5 points. Team corrections start after 3 graded games for a team.

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total within its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 34.3 points), no bet.
